scenario.name: Google Cloud Security, Wiz & MITRE — GCP Cloud Build Default Service Account & Artifact Registry Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a cloud software factory whose automated build bay runs every submitted assembly job wearing a generously powered default factory badge that holds keys to both the artifact vault and the source storage warehouse. Submitting an ad-hoc build order containing one sneaky command, an intruder walks into the worker booth, reads the default factory badge straight off the wall metadata box, and uses it to raid both finished packages and private source archives. In this scenario (T1648, Google Cloud Security, Wiz & MITRE, GCP Cloud Build Default Service Account & Artifact Registry Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: submitting Ad-Hoc Cloud Build Job, then worker Container Metadata Query, then artifact Registry. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Submitting Ad-Hoc Cloud Build Job, then Worker Container Metadata Query, then Artifact Registry, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1648 across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Disable the legacy default Cloud Build Service Account privilege assignment via Organization Policy constraints/cloudbuild.useBuildServiceAccount and require user-specified least-privilege service accounts per build trigger.

stages.title: Stage 1: Submitting Ad-Hoc Cloud Build Job via google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1648 - Serverless Execution)
stages.description: Using compromised developer permissions that allow triggering builds, the intruder submits a quick custom assembly job straight to the cloud build queue carrying an inline shell step designed purely to harvest credentials. A compromised identity holding roles/cloudbuild.builds.editor (or cloudbuild.builds.create) submits an inline cloudbuild.yaml build step via gcloud builds submit, recorded in GCP Admin Activity Cloud Audit Logs (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with GcpService=cloudbuild.googleapis.com, MethodName=google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild, CallerPrincipal=dev-ci-user@corp-prod-01.iam.gserviceaccount.com so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild"' --limit=10 (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.Create so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1648 during "Submitting Ad-Hoc Cloud Build Job via google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact gcloud builds describe <build-id> runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud builds describe <build-id> against AWS CloudTrail, GCP Cloud Audit, or Microsoft Entra so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1648 during "Submitting Ad-Hoc Cloud Build Job via google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild / ⇠#1 ACK 200) from Node ① (#1 Developer Role (cloudbuild.builds.create)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Artifact Registry & GCS Storage Buckets).

keySpecs.value: Disable the legacy default Cloud Build Service Account privilege assignment via Organization Policy constraints/cloudbuild.useBuildServiceAccount and require user-specified least-privilege service accounts per build trigger.

stages.title: Stage 2: Worker Container Metadata Query for @cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com OAuth2 Token
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1552.005 - Cloud Instance Metadata API)
stages.description: The moment the automated build bay spins up the attacker worker container, the container taps the booth local metadata wall panel and lifts the live OAuth badge belonging to the overly privileged default Cloud Build service account. Inside the Cloud Build step container, the build command queries http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token (with header Metadata-Flavor: Google) to retrieve the OAuth2 access token of <project-number>@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with MetadataEndpoint=http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token, InheritedIdentity=445566778899@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com, BuildStepImage=gcr.io/cloud-builders/gcloud so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes gcloud projects get-iam-policy corp-prod-01 --flatten="bindings[].members" --filter="bindings.members:cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com" (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud projects get-iam-policy corp-prod-01 --flatten="bindings[].members" --filter="bindings so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1552.005 during "Worker Container Metadata Query for @cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com OAuth2 Token" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact gcloud logging read 'resource.type="build"' --limit=20 runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud logging read 'resource.type="build"' --limit=20 against AWS CloudTrail, GCP Cloud Audi so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1552.005 during "Worker Container Metadata Query for @cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com OAuth2 Token" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ curl -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 GCP Cloud Build API (builds.create)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Artifact Registry & GCS Storage Buckets).

keySpecs.value: Remove broad roles/editor or roles/cloudbuild.builds.builder permissions from the default <project-number>@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com identity and enforce VPC Service Controls around Cloud Build worker pools.

stages.title: Stage 3: Artifact Registry & Cloud Storage Source Archive Access Audit
stages.subtitle: Collection (T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage)
stages.description: Wielding the stolen default builder badge, the intruder opens both the finished-software Artifact Registry and the private Cloud Storage source archives to steal proprietary builds or plant tampered release images. Using the Cloud Build service account token, the actor reads container images in Artifact Registry and staging archives in gs://<project>_cloudbuild/source/, logged in GCP Data Access Audit Logs (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with AuditLogStream=cloudaudit.googleapis.com/data_access, MethodName=storage.objects.get, TargetBucketObject=gs://corp-prod-01_cloudbuild/source/1763312400.tgz so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="445566778899@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com" AND logName:"cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Fdata_access"' (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="445566778899@cloudbuild. so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1530 during "Artifact Registry & Cloud Storage Source Archive Access Audit" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact gcloud iam service-accounts disable 445566778899@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud iam service-accounts disable 445566778899@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com against AWS C so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1530 during "Artifact Registry & Cloud Storage Source Archive Access Audit" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ storage.objects.get on buckets/corp-prod-01_cloudbuild/objects/source/archive.tgz / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 GCP Cloud Build API (builds.create)) to Node ④ (#4 Cloud Build Worker Metadata Server), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Artifact Registry & GCS Storage Buckets).

keySpecs.value: Enable GCP Data Access Audit Logs (DATA_READ / DATA_WRITE) for Cloud Storage and Artifact Registry and monitor Security Command Center (SCC) for anomalous Cloud Build Service Account calls from outside Google IP space.
